videos.script: The bookshop runs on a server. From the outside, a process that works and a process that is stuck look the same. {{blackbox}} The operating system knows the process exists. It does not know whether the database still answers, or whether orders are failing. {{inside}} Spring Boot Actuator lets the application say so itself. It adds endpoints that answer questions about the application, not about books. {{endpoints}} In this lesson you put them on a port of their own, which only the machine itself can reach. {{port}} You ask the bookshop whether it is healthy. Then you take its database away, and watch the answer change. {{health}} You meet the two questions an orchestrator asks. Are you alive? Are you ready? They have different answers, and a wrong answer to either costs something different. {{probes}} Then you count things. Requests, connections in the pool, and orders refused for lack of stock. {{metrics}} And you read the same numbers the way Prometheus collects them, and decide which of them should wake somebody up. {{alert}}
